newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar falls sharply against mark by late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar falls sharply against mark by late Tokyo.

text.p: The dollar fell sharply against the mark by late afternoon on Monday after traders, mostly overseas speculators, sold dollars for marks to cut losses on their long positions, dealers said.
Dollar sales against the German unit caused a fall in dollar/yen rates in tandem, but the greenback was supported near 1.70 marks and 125 yen during Asian trading time.
The dollar lost over 100 points or one pfennig against mark, falling as low as 1.7004 marks by late afternoon Tokyo after earlier rising to 1.7129 marks.

The mark's renewed strength against major currencies was partly caused by pessimism over European economic and monetary union (EMU) due to possible French general elections and a news report over the weekend that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) had criticised Italy's proposed mini-budget for lacking structural reform measures, currency traders said.
"Today's (overall) trade is mainly dominated by the mark's movements," a city bank dealer said.

Political sources in France said President Jacques Chirac would end a week of feverish speculation by announcing in a televised address expected at 8 p.m. (1800 GMT) on Monday that a two-round general election would be held either May 25-June 1 or June 1-8. Chirac's office had refused to confirm this.
Opinion polls predict a close battle. The National Assembly, where the ruling centre-right has a massive majority, does not officially have to face the electorate until March 1998.

A trust bank dealer said the mark had been bought back in reaction to the weekend reports, adding that he would watch closely how European traders react to the mark's strength in European trading time.

During the morning, the dollar slid after stop-loss sales were set off at 1.7080 and 1.7050 marks, which also weighed on the dollar against the yen. In addition, Japanese investors were deteced behind dollar sales vs the yen around 125.70 yen.
But the mark's strength against the yen and bids from Japanese investors and importers below 125 yen supported the dollar against the yen, dealers said.

The mark rose to around 73.77 yen after stop-loss buying was touched off near 73.70 yen, but stood at around 73.64/67 yen at 0713 GMT after profit-taking kicked in and eroded earlier gains. It had been around 73.52 yen in early Tokyo.
Dealers in Singapore said the dollar's upside vs the yen was capped by last week's remarks by Finance Ministry official Sakakibara hinting at a possible Japanese interest rate rise.

Some traders in Tokyo said a fall below 125 yen is possible if the dollar edges down versus the mark and triggers stop-loss sales below 1.70 marks. -- Singapore newsroom +65-8703083, Yoko Nishikawa in Tokyo +81-3-3432-8584
